# bugs #3895: mcs51: internal error in SDCCmem.c for a 128-byte char array with an initializer

- Ticket: https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/bugs/3895/
- Category: [Not reproducible](../../not-reproducible.md)
- Evidence: tested on r17176
- Recommended action: Close as not reproducible on r17176. local 0002 has other input that fails at the same assertion.

## Finding

The attachment `main.c` compiles on r17176 with the options of the ticket, which are
`-mmcs51 --opt-code-size --fverbose-asm -c`. The compiler prints no message and returns exit
status 0. The result is the same when one of `--model-medium`, `--model-large`, `--model-huge`,
`--stack-auto`, `--stack-auto --xstack`, and `--nooverlay` is added to these options. Variants of
the file compile with the options of the ticket as well: arrays of 200 and of 300 elements, an
`int` array, an `__idata` array, and a string literal as the initializer. Linking the file with an
empty `main` function gives a regular diagnostic, which is what the author of the first comment
expects.

    ?ASlink-Error-Could not get 128 consecutive bytes in internal RAM for area DSEG.

The reporter used revision 15257 on a MinGW64 host. The tests for this entry ran on a Linux host
with a compiler built from r17176. A MinGW host and r15257 were not tested. The revision after
which the file compiles was not identified.

Line 1292 of `src/SDCCmem.c` in r15257 is `wassert (currFunc)` in `canOverlayLocals`. The assertion
fails when the overlay segment has a symbol while no function is being compiled. The mcs51
register allocator adds such a symbol when it spills a temporary in the code that initializes a
global variable. Warning 84 in the ticket names a temporary, `iTemp254`, on the line of the array.

## Related

local 0002 has three initializers that fail with the small model on r17176. For the first the
compiler fails at this assertion. For the second it writes assembly that the assembler rejects, and
for the third it ends with a segmentation fault.
